name: Jahleel
overview: Jahleel is a male figure from the tribe of Zebulun, identified specifically as a son of Zebulun. He appears in the biblical record as part of the list of sons of Israel who went to Egypt, highlighting his role within the early patriarchal history. His descendants formed the Jahleelites, a clan mentioned in the book of Numbers.
namesAndTitles: The name Jahleel means 'wait for God' or possibly 'may God show himself friendly,' reflecting a hopeful trust in God's character. This proper name, given in Genesis 46:14, carries a spiritual significance tied to reliance on the Lord.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jahleel as a son of Zebulun, establishing his place within the family of Israel. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jahleel's importance lies in his inclusion among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking the continuation of the covenant family during a critical period of preservation and growth. His lineage, the Jahleelites, represents one of the clans within the tribe of Zebulun, contributing to the tribal structure of Israel as recorded in Numbers. This connection underscores God's faithfulness in maintaining the descendants of Israel through generations.
